body.text: write in the second person, present tense, active voice.
acknowledge what happened in one sentence before anything else.
use the customer's own words for the problem when quoting it back.
open with an apology for the delay before saying what you will do.

If a sentence would survive being read aloud to the customer's manager,
it is probably fine. If it would not, rewrite it.

Ask one question per message. If you need three answers, ask the most
blocking one first and say the others will follow.

entries.definition:
A tracked customer request. Never "issue" — that word is for engineering,
and customers hear it as blame.

Handing a ticket to a human. Say so in the reply, and say when they will
answer.

A way to get the outcome without the fix. Always label it as one, so the
customer knows the fix is still coming.

body.text:
Your export stopped at 40% around 09:10 your time — I can see it in the
logs. Here's what I'm doing about it.

The export will finish overnight; I'll confirm here by 08:00 tomorrow.
Nothing you need to do until then.

Every agent that writes to a customer includes this file. It is versioned
and published separately, so a change to voice reaches every agent at the
next delivery without editing any of them.
